subject: literature
passage: Rafael had played his audition piece for the city orchestra that morning, and the results would be posted at six o'clock. By five, he had tuned his violin twice, though he had no plans to play it, and had reread the same page of his book so many times that he could not have said what it was about. Every few minutes, he glanced at the clock on the wall. These details suggest that Rafael ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: was confident that he had already won a place in the orchestra.
choices.B: had lost interest in music after a difficult audition.
choices.C: was too anxious about the results to focus on anything else.
choices.D: was hoping to practice once more before the results appeared.

explanation.why: Rafael keeps doing pointless tasks, cannot take in what he reads, and checks the clock again and again while waiting for the results. These are signs of nervous waiting.
explanation.A: Incorrect. His restless behavior shows worry, not calm confidence.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing suggests he has lost interest in music; he is eagerly waiting for the results.
explanation.C: Correct. Retuning an instrument he will not play, rereading without understanding, and watching the clock all show anxiety.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says he had no plans to play the violin.
